extracted.intended_audience: general online readers interested in media, journalism, and current events (Bustle readership)
extracted.subtask_short: news coverage of retracted magazine article
extracted.subtask_description: A short online news piece reporting that a long-form magazine article was retracted and summarizing what went wrong in its editorial process. It explains the retraction, independent review findings, and where the original text can still be read.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic, even routine journalistic practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The Columbia School of Journalism concluded the article failed "basic, even routine journalistic practice" in its reporting and fact-checking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used by the piece to summarize the core failing identified by the review; implies expectation that standard journalistic procedures (source verification, corroboration, clear note of uncertainties) should be followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting rigor
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of reporting — how thoroughly reporters gather, corroborate, and present facts (the report found serious gaps 'from reporting to writing, fact-checking, and verification').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes ensuring multiple corroborating sources where appropriate, careful interviewing, and avoiding overreliance on a single unverified account; the article references the Washington Post finding 'holes in the account' as an example of inadequate reporting rigor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fact-checking
rubrics_metrics.description: The process of verifying factual claims before publication — the Columbia review found failures specifically in fact-checking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expectations include checking details with independent records or witnesses, confirming timelines and assertions, and updating or retracting when factual errors are discovered; the piece cites the magazine's apology that outlined specific discrepancies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of sources/accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Corroboration and scrutiny of a source's account — the story noted 'holes in the account offered by Jackie' and that lack of evidence does not necessarily disprove an allegation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters should seek corroborating evidence and be transparent about what is and is not verified; anonymous or pseudonymous sources require additional care to corroborate their claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial oversight and review
rubrics_metrics.description: Processes within the publication that ensure pieces meet standards — the magazine asked Columbia's journalism school to review its 'editorial practice' after concerns arose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes internal fact-checking workflows, editor involvement, and willingness to commission independent reviews when systemic problems are suspected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency, corrections, and reader communication
rubrics_metrics.description: How the publication communicates errors and corrections — Rolling Stone 'issued a note to its readers, apologizing for the flawed story and outlining specific discrepancies' and attached an editor's note to the original story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best practice: promptly notify readers of errors, explain what was wrong and what was done to investigate, and make corrections, retractions, or editor's notes clearly visible and linked to the original content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archiving and public record (preservation of original text)
rubrics_metrics.description: Even when removed, online content can remain accessible via archives — the Internet Archive's Wayback Machine captured 300 versions of the original story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes the role of archival tools in preserving publishing history and enabling later review of original reporting and editorial changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible reporting on sexual assault and victim consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Balancing investigative standards with sensitivity to alleged victims — the article notes the haunting nature of Jackie's account and cautions that mishandling one story 'should not silence those stories and others from coming forward.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists should verify claims without retraumatizing or silencing victims; maintain sensitivity while upholding verification standards and ensuring fair treatment of all parties.
